mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has improved monotonically from -12.4% to -10.7% over four weeks, signaling gradual return-to-office behavior. This sustained trend will continue driving weekday retail visits as commuters resume shopping routines, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 1.7 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses direction by more than 2 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has declined from 7.7% to 4.6% over four weeks, indicating reduced home-confinement behavior and increased outdoor activity willingness. This behavioral shift will translate to higher retail-and-recreation visits as residents normalize out-of-home consumption patterns.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 3.1 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 6.0% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC declines further in the next two weeks despite lower residential confinement.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility remains severely depressed at -34.4%, constraining access to retail clusters. If TRANSIT recovers by more than 5 percentage points within two weeks, the removal of this access constraint will unlock retail-and-recreation mobility gains.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT remains below -30% for the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite TRANSIT recovery.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility is severely suppressed at -35.0%, indicating outdoor recreation constraints. Concurrent low TRANSIT (-34.4%) and low WORKPLACES (-10.7%) create a regime where retail-and-recreation is suppressed by lack of foot traffic from both commuting and park-based leisure. Recovery requires simultaneous improvement in both TRANSIT and PARKS.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and TRANSIT both remain below -30%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -35.0% and TRANSIT at -34.4% in t-0w
failure_condition: Either PARKS or TRANSIT recovers above -25% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC subsequently rises, contradicting the interaction hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September in Madrid marks the end of summer vacation season. Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility has stabilized near +1.6%, indicating return-to-routine consumption. This seasonal normalization will extend to retail-and-recreation as back-to-school and autumn shopping patterns activate over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable at +1.6% to +1.9% across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the prior 28-day mean, or GROCERY_PHARM declines below 0% in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Transit mobility at -34.4% suggests ongoing mobility restrictions or service disruptions. If restrictions tighten further (TRANSIT falls below -40%), retail-and-recreation will decline as access to shopping venues becomes more constrained. Conversely, if restrictions ease (TRANSIT rises above -30%), retail recovery will accelerate.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -40% in week t+1
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined from -35.9% to -34.4% over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below -40% but RETAIL_REC increases in the following week, or TRANSIT remains between -40% and -30% and RETAIL_REC does not respond directionally.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of stable GROCERY_PHARM (+1.6%) and declining RESIDENTIAL (4.6%) indicates residents are leaving home for essential shopping but not yet for discretionary retail. If WORKPLACES continues its recovery trend and RESIDENTIAL stabilizes below 5%, discretionary retail visits will increase as confidence in out-of-home activity normalizes.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains below 5.5% AND WORKPLACES improves by more than 1 percentage point
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 6.0% in week t+1, or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 1 percentage point, or RETAIL_REC declines despite meeting both trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility at -35.0% reflects suppressed outdoor leisure activity. If parks mobility recovers above -25% within one week, this signals removal of outdoor activity constraints and will immediately boost retail-and-recreation as residents engage in shopping-adjacent leisure trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -25% in week t+1
failure_condition: PARKS rises above -25% in week t+1 but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the same week, or PARKS remains below -30% for the next two weeks.
